articles.title: PVL: Nxled fends off Ho Chi Minh City to stay in race to final
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Nxled turned back Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City, 25-20, 31-33, 25-17, 25-22, to stay in finals contention in the PVL Invitational Conference on Friday at Smart Araneta Coliseum.…

blocks.text: Nxled Chameleons’ Jonah Sabete-Escamillan rises for a hit during a game vs Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City in the PVL Invitational Conference. –MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net
MANILA, Philippines — Nxled turned back Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City, 25-20, 31-33, 25-17, 25-22, to stay in finals contention in the PVL Invitational Conference on Friday at Smart Araneta Coliseum.

Jonah Sabete-Escamillan continued to display an all-around game with 18 points, 20 excellent receptions, and 15 digs. Myla Pablo also scored 18, highlighted by five blocks, while MJ Phillips chipped in 17 points.
Gel Cayuna dished out 35 excellent sets, as EJ Laure-Cariño had 16 points and 24 excellent receptions, while Jackie Acuña added 12, as Nxled tied PLDT at 2-2.
Nxled, which battles Farm Fresh on Sunday at 1:30 p.m., holds the tie-break advantage with seven points ahead of PLDT’s six.

Hours after a five-set meltdown to EST Cola on Thursday night when they blew a 20-12 lead in the fourth set, the Chameleons squandered another big lead against the Vietnamese, who erased their 19-10 margin and cut it down to one, 22-21, after Dang Thi Kim Thanh’s kill.

blocks.caption: Nxled Chameleons during a game vs Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City in the PVL Invitational Conference.

blocks.text: Nxled Chameleons during a game vs Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City in the PVL Invitational Conference. –MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net
Phillips and Escamillan refused to suffer the same heartbreak, closing out the game with three points including two quick attacks from the former.

“We love to fight because the last game was a five set and it was only a few hours ago. It was really tough and we wanted immediately to show that we never back down, we are not broken, we will never be broken after a losing match and we are ready to fight,” said Nxled coach Ettore Guidetti.

“Obviously, there are bad things and good things. The good thing is this one: we never give up. The bad thing is that we are developing the side out, but we can do even better because sometimes, I joke about this, our side out is kind of bipolar or we play like a super great team or we get scared and under pressure and nothing works, and so it’s a part of the mental game that we have to really develop.”
Dang led the Vietnamese with 15 points and 15 digs. The 16-year-old Ho Thi Bich Diep had 13 points, while Dao Thi Nhung added 11.
Ho Chi Minh bombed out of finals contention with a 1-3 record.

articles.title: Romanian prosecutors indict influencer Andrew Tate for trafficking minors, money laundering
articles.summary: Romanian prosecutors officially indicted social media influencer Andrew Tate on Friday for trafficking minors, money laundering, sex with a minor and witness tampering and his brother Tristan for…

image.caption: Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan Tate talk to the media outside their residence on March 23, 2025 in Bucharest, Romania. The brothers were officially indicted by Romanian prosecutors on Friday. (Andrei Pungovschi/Getty Images)

blocks.text: World·New

Romanian prosecutors officially indicted social media influencer Andrew Tate on Friday for trafficking minors, money laundering, sex with a minor and witness tampering and his brother Tristan for complicity, years after they began investigating them.
His brother Tristan was also indicted for complicity, in criminal investigation that began in 2022
The Tate brothers, former kickboxers with dual U.S. and British ​citizenship, were arrested in Miami in late July after Britain requested their extradition.
Mainly based in Romania since 2017, they have been under criminal investigation in the country since December 2022 on charges including human trafficking. They have denied all wrongdoing.

Romanian prosecutors said the Tates recruited their victims by seducing them and falsely claiming to want a relationship or marriage, before forcing them to produce pornographic content for a webcam business.

"We will examine every aspect of [the indictment] with the same level of scrutiny and we will challenge any evidential, procedural or legal deficiencies through the appropriate judicial process," a Romanian lawyer for the Tates, Eugen Vidineac, said in a statement.
"Our clients continue to reject the allegations against them."
The criminal case against Andrew Tate | About That
The Tate brothers remain in jail in the U.S. while a judge decides on the request for their extradition to Britain, where they are wanted on rape charges.

The spokesperson for the Romanian anti-organized crime prosecuting unit DIICOT — which is investigating the Tates — said it was not immediately clear whether the unit will seek their extradition from the United States.

The Tates can be tried in absentia in Romania, but the trial will not start immediately. Under Romanian law, the indictment gets sent to a preliminary court chamber, where a judge will inspect the case files to ensure legality.

items: Tate brothers to fight extradition to U.K., where both face charges of rape
How Andrew Tate made abuse a business

blocks.text: While the law states that the preliminary chamber judge has 60 days to finalize the report, indictments routinely take significantly longer.
Andrew Tate, a self-described misogynist, previously said he moved to Romania because law enforcement was more lax there.
Both brothers have grown their following of mainly young men by building a lavish, hyper-macho image of driving fast cars and dating beautiful women.

articles.title: Dalaguete vegetable farmer on motorbike shot, killed
articles.summary: A 29-year-old farmer was shot dead in a violent ambush while driving his motorcycle loaded with baskets of fresh vegetables on Thursday evening, September 3, in Barangay Nalhub, Dalaguete, Cebu....…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A 29-year-old farmer was shot dead in a violent ambush while driving his motorcycle loaded with baskets of fresh vegetables on Thursday evening, September 3, in Barangay Nalhub, Dalaguete, Cebu.

Police identified the victim as alias “JR,” a farmer and resident of Barangay Nalhub. Investigators confirmed that the victim died instantly at the scene after sustaining multiple gunshot wounds to various parts of his body.
The incident occurred around 7:15 p.m. while the victim was transporting his produce along the road.
The Dalaguete Municipal Police Station immediately launched an investigation after receiving a call from the Barangay Chairman of Nalhub reporting the shooting.
Initial police findings revealed that the victim was actively maneuvering his motorcycle—which was carrying vegetable baskets (locally known as bukag)—when he was fired upon.
Probe in progress
At the crime scene, forensic investigators recovered two empty shell casings believed to be from a .45 caliber handgun, as well as two misfired rounds of ammunition.
The perpetrator remains unidentified and fled the scene following the attack.
The Dalaguete Police are continuing their investigation to determine the motive and trace the whereabouts of the suspect.

articles.title: Cebuana Lhuillier turns purposeful communication into impact at the Philippine Quill Awards
articles.summary: Cebuana Lhuillier is demonstrating how strategic communication can go beyond telling a company’s story to creating value for the people it reaches. Through its workplace, financial education,…

blocks.text: Cebuana Lhuillier is demonstrating how strategic communication can go beyond telling a company’s story to creating value for the people it reaches. Through its workplace, financial education, entrepreneurship, and advocacy platforms, the company uses communication to address real needs, create opportunities, and encourage people to learn, participate, and take action.

This approach earned the company Merit recognition at the 22nd Philippine Quill Awards across four areas: Internal Communication for Amazing KaCebuana; Corporate Social Responsibility for Money Guro and Happiest Pinoy; Government Relations and Public Affairs for its range of Business Support solutions; and Social Media for Money Guro.

For Cebuana Lhuillier President and CEO Jean Henri Lhuillier, effective communication should create value for the people it reaches. “At Cebuana Lhuillier, communication is not just about telling people what we do. It is about creating something useful for the people we serve,” said Lhuillier. “When communication helps an employee feel valued, gives a Filipino knowledge to make better decisions, equips an entrepreneur to grow, or gives people a reason to believe in themselves and each other, then it has done its job.”
Purpose Across Every Platform
That principle is reflected in each of the company’s recognized initiatives, with every platform built around a distinct audience need.

Within the organization, Amazing KaCebu integrates employee engagement into the everyday work experience. Through platforms such as Workvivo and the Corporate News Ngayon newsletter, which connects thousands of employees across the country, along with the Brillo Awards, leadership programs, and the REBEL wellbeing app, employees have more ways to stay informed, be recognized, be heard, and feel supported.

For navigating everyday financial decisions, Money Guro makes financial education more accessible and relatable by turning complex concepts into practical conversations. Through social media, student engagements, workshops, and even Roblox, it brings financial education closer to Filipinos.

Happiest Pinoy takes a different approach, using storytelling to reflect the Filipino experience. Its 2025 campaign moved beyond the search for a single “happiest” Filipino and opened the platform to stories of hope, recovery, and resilience, giving people space to share experiences and find connection through a shared sense of community.

For entrepreneurs, Cebuana Lhuillier’s suite of business support solutions recognizes that capital is only one part of what MSMEs need to grow. Its digital-first ecosystem brings together business education, expert guidance, tools, mentoring, entrepreneur stories, and financial services to help business owners make better decisions and build capability at every stage of their journey.
What connects these initiatives is a simple approach: start with what people need, then find the right way to reach them.

“What makes these initiatives stand out is how each one starts with a clear audience need and translates it into a communication approach that people can relate to and act on,” said Emirosco Michael Sena, First Vice President and Chief Marketing and Communications Officer of Cebuana Lhuillier. “Whether we are engaging our employees, simplifying financial concepts, supporting entrepreneurs, or telling stories of resilience, we look at the right message, platform, and format for each audience. The Merit Awards validate that approach and the work of our teams in turning strong ideas into programs that deliver results.”
Communication That Moves People

Organized by the International Association of Business Communicators (IABC) Philippines, the Philippine Quill Awards recognize excellence in business communication, including strategic thinking, creative execution, and results.

For Cebuana Lhuillier, the recognition reinforces the role communication can play beyond corporate messaging. Done with purpose, it can help employees feel connected, make knowledge more accessible, strengthen entrepreneurs, and create space for stories that matter.
Ultimately, the goal is not simply to be heard. It is to create communication that leaves people with something they can use, act on, or carry forward.
ADVT.
This article is brought to you by Cebuana Lhuillier.

articles.title: Philippines’ defense dep’t hits China’s ‘state-sponsored propaganda’ claiming Batanes
articles.summary: State-run Global Times runs an opinion piece claiming Batanes is part of China — a claim Chinese academics first put forward in late June 2026

blocks.text: NORTHERNMOST OUTPOST. The Philippine Flag proudly stands in Mavulis Island, Batanes province in this AFP handout from October 2023.
Armed Forces of the Philippines
State-run Global Times runs an opinion piece claiming Batanes is part of China — a claim Chinese academics first put forward in late June 2026

items: The Philippines' Department of National Defense condemned claims by a Chinese publication that Batanes is part of China, asserting that such narratives are false and a violation of Philippine sovereignty.
The National Historical Commission of the Philippines refuted the claims, stating that Batanes has always been part of the Philippines and has no historical ties to China or Taiwan.
Batanes is strategically important due to its proximity to Taiwan and critical maritime routes.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The Philippines’ Department of National Defense (DND) on Friday, September 4, condemned “state-sponsored propaganda” that claims Batanes is part of China.

“Patunay lamang ito sa patuloy na pagpapakalat ng Tsina ng mga baluktot na naratibo sa buong mundo (This is further proof that China continues to push a false narrative),” said the DND, which has administrative oversight of the Philippine military, among the frontliners in Manila’s defense of its maritime rights and entitlements.

On Thursday, September 3, the Chinese Communist Party-linked tabloid Global Times published an opinion piece titled “History shows that Batanes Islands do not belong to the Philippines,” written by Wang Yuanyuan, who is identified as an assistant research fellow at the Hainan-based Center for South China Sea History and Culture.

“Hindi kailanman naging bahagi ng Tsina ang Batanes o anumang lugar sa Pilipinas, at kailanman ay hindi natin hahayaan ang anumang pagtatangka sa soberanya at teritoryo ng Republika ng Pilipinas (Neither Batanes nor any other part of the Philippines has been part of China. We will not allow any attempts to violate the sovereignty and territory of the Philippines),” added the DND.
In a separate statement, Philippine Coast Guard spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela also criticized the opinion piece.

“Manufacturing a dispute where none exists does not create one. It only tells us what Beijing intends,” said Tarriela, who, alongside Defense chief Gilberto Teodoro Jr., is among the loudest voices in the Philippines not only on Beijing’s encroachments in the West Philippine Sea and other maritime areas, but also against what security and defense experts have pinpointed as China’s malign and disinformation operations on the Philippines.

The opinion piece, which is just under 700 words long, claims that treaties that defined the Philippines following colonization supposedly “excluded” the Batanes Islands, the northernmost part of the Philippine archipelago. Wang also claimed “illegal United States expansion” and supposed “historical and cultural ties to Taiwan” as the basis for his claim that Batanes is part of China.

The narrative that Batanes, a province with just under 19,000, based on the Philippines’ last 2024 census, is part of China is new but also persistent. It was only last June when supposed Chinese scholars who met at an academic symposium at Jinan University “unanimously concluded that the Batan Islands constitute a natural geographic extension of Taiwan.”
China claims independently governed Taiwan, formally known as the Republic of China, even if the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) has never ruled over the island.
The National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) has denied claims made by the Chinese scholar, noting the following in a July 2026 statement:

items: Batanes isn’t an extension of Taiwan. On the flip side, “current satellite and oceanographic data by the Philippines and other nations clearly show a continuous shelf extending from Northern Luzon through the Babuyan & Batanes Islands, and into parts of the Taiwan archipelago.” “The Philippines claims a greater right over the subject territories from this perspective,” said the NHCP.

Batanes’ history is as Filipino as it gets. The NHCP rejected supposed historical ties that trace back to ancient times. The earliest known documentation of the Batanes Islands in 1687 by British explorer William Dampier, said the NHCP, “noted no trace of Chinese governance over the islands.” The Ivatan, natives of Batanes, traded extensively with other maritime people. Batanes was part of Cagayan province when the Spanish claimed sovereignty over the Philippine archipelago. Ivatans revolted against the Spanish, too. “Since 1783, the Philippine government and its legal predecessors have held continuous and undisputed sovereignty over Batanes…. They were represented in the Malolos Congress and every subsequent iteration of our national legislature. They have an elected government, one that is recognized by the whole world as Filipino.”

Batanes was not for the Japanese to hand over to China. “On the claim that the Batanes Islands were part of the territory that was to be returned to China by Japan following the end of the Second World War, Japan cannot give to China what clearly belongs to the Philippines. Furthermore, the people of Batanes had already liberated themselves from Japanese rule by early 1945. This only proves beyond any doubt that Batanes has always been Filipino.”

blocks.text: Experts had long flagged the Jinan University symposium, and its supposed findings, over fears that the CCP and Chinese government would eventually use those assertions as a basis for claiming Batanes, too.

The islands of Batanes, aside from being the land of the Ivatans, are in a very strategic location. Its proximity to Taiwan means it’s a critical or vulnerable area should Beijing force a “unification” with Taiwan through force. It also lies on the other side of the Bashi Channel, a critical waterway for undersea cables and maritime traffic.
The Philippine military has, in recent years, slowly improved its facilities and presence in Batanes precisely because of its strategic importance.
Both soldiers from the Philippines and its allies have trained in the province, including on Mavulis Island, the northernmost island in the Philippines. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Zheng Qinwen back in the hunt–and US Open third round
articles.summary: NEW YORK– Zheng Qinwen flopped to the court then jumped up in a fist-pumping celebration Thursday after battling into the US Open third round, the 2024 Olympic gold medalist relishing the return of…

blocks.text: FILE–Qinwen Zheng of China. (AP Photo/Maja Smiejkowska)

NEW YORK– Zheng Qinwen flopped to the court then jumped up in a fist-pumping celebration Thursday after battling into the US Open third round, the 2024 Olympic gold medalist relishing the return of her game — and her competitive fire.
The former world number four endured an injury-plagued 2025 that included a longer than anticipated recovery from elbow surgery.
She missed the Australian Open and has struggled to regain her form, and the mindset of a champion.
“Before the surgery, for me winning is like drinking water — everything comes natural, everything comes fluent,” Zheng said after beating Yulia Putintseva 6-4, 2-6, 6-1 to reach the third round.
“After my surgery, I had some tough matches against the best players in the world (and) I’m close but I don’t get them.
“I totally lost the dynamic of how to compete.
“Now after two, three months I really felt the first time in this tournament I find myself, I found my fire back during the competition.”
Zheng sank so far in the rankings that she had to go through qualifying to book her US Open berth.
She grudgingly acknowledged that grinding through the qualifiers may have helped her regain her competitive edge — but that didn’t really take the sting away.
“It takes a while for me to accept my ranking dropped to 125 and, OK, I need to actually play qualies,” she said.
Now she’s in the thick of the main draw and will face former Australian Open champion Keys for a place in the last 16.
Zheng is looking forward to the test — and likely a chance to step back onto one of the main show courts of Flushing Meadows after toiling through two rounds on the outside courts.
“I used to always play on the big court,” she said. “I need to fight to get everything back.”

articles.title: Over half of targeted kinds injected vs measles, rubella in Ilocos Region
articles.summary: SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — A total of 272,096 children, or 61.2 percent of the target population, have been vaccinated against measles and rubella in the Ilocos Region as of Sept. 2, according to…

blocks.text: SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — A total of 272,096 children, or 61.2 percent of the target population, have been vaccinated against measles and rubella in the Ilocos Region as of Sept. 2, according to the latest “Ligtas Tigdas” bulletin.
The vaccination campaign covers children aged 6 months to 59 months across the region.
Among the age groups, children aged 24 to 59 months accounted for the largest number of vaccinated at 186,926, representing 63 percent coverage.
This was followed by 50,180 vaccinated children aged 13 to 23 months, or 55.6 percent, and 34,900 children vaccinated aged 6 to 12 months, or 60.7 percent.
Ilocos Norte posted the highest coverage at 90.2 percent, with 38,442 children vaccinated.
Ilocos Sur followed with 40,657 vaccinated, or 83.5 percent coverage, while La Union recorded 42,586 or 68 percent.
Pangasinan had 139,307 vaccinated children, equivalent to 50.6 percent coverage, while Dagupan City recorded 11,104 or 72.2 percent.
Several local governments have already surpassed the 95-percent measles-rubella vaccination coverage target.
Batac City in Ilocos Norte was the first city in the region to reach the target, recording 98 percent coverage.
Among municipalities, Currimao led with 105.5 percent, followed by Dingras at 105.1 percent and Carasi at 104.2 percent.
Bantay in Ilocos Sur recorded 101 percent, while Marcos posted 97.5 percent, Piddig 96.4 percent, Solsona 96.1 percent, Pinili 96 percent and Pagudpud 95.7 percent.
Health authorities encourage parents and guardians to have eligible children vaccinated as the campaign seeks to increase protection against measles and rubella across the region. /apl
—Kenneth P. Tabin / Contributor

articles.title: Yvon Bisera shooting for two birds at LPGT Summit Point stop
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines–In-form Yvon Bisera seeks a third Ladies PGT title this season, teeing off as the solid favorite when the ICTSI Summit Point Championship gets off the ground Tuesday in Lipa City…

blocks.text: Yvon Bisera has two wins in the LPGT season thus far. CONTRIBUTED PHOTO

MANILA, Philippines–In-form Yvon Bisera seeks a third Ladies PGT title this season, teeing off as the solid favorite when the ICTSI Summit Point Championship gets off the ground Tuesday in Lipa City in Batangas.
Bisera will not just be seeking to win another P1 million event, but also use this stint to sharpen her game for a first appearance in the lucrative yet tougher Korean LPGA later this month.

“I want to play well at Summit Point and use it to prepare for Korea,” said Bisera, who will play in the Hana Financial Group Championship from Sept. 17-20 in Gyeonggi Province, on Daebudo Island southwest of Seoul.

Bisera has been in impressive form on the LPGT this season, outlasting two rivals in a playoff to capture the Lakewood Championship in March. She then produced an emphatic seven-shot victory at the Pradera Verde Championship last July, and those victories have certainly established her as a favorite in Lipa.
With her Korean LPGA debut fast approaching, Bisera has used her time between tournaments to fine-tune the part of her game she believes could prove decisive at Summit Point: the short game.

While waiting for her Korean visa documents, the Davaoeña has devoted extra time to sharpening her touch around the greens, particularly with the possibility of strong winds adding another layer of difficulty at the Batangas layout.
“You can’t lose focus at Summit Point, especially in the face of strong winds,” Bisera continued in Filipino.
That focus will be particularly crucial in a 54-hole event, where a fast start can provide early advantage.
Bisera, however, is not expecting another runaway performance like the one she produced at Pradera Verde.
“I really want to win, but everyone in the field has been preparing hard for this tournament,” she said. “But I will try my best to perform well for my confidence going to Korea.”

She will have plenty of opposition in Batangas, with reigning Order of Merit champion Sarah Ababa leading a compact but formidable field that also features former leg winners Mafy Singson, Tiffany Lee, Chihiro Ikeda and Princess Superal.

Korean challenger Kim Seoyun is likewise expected to figure prominently, along with title-hungry contenders Martina Miñoza, Pamela Mariano, Velinda Castil, Rev Alcantara, Angela Mangana and Gretchen Villacencio.

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — A pedestrian and a motorcycle rider died in separate road accidents in Rizal province on Thursday, Sept. 3, police said.
The Calabarzon police, in a report on Friday. (September 4), said the a road mishap happened along Marcos Highway in Barangay San Jose at Antipolo City in the early hours of Thursday.
A 22-year-old motorcycle rider was traveling when he reportedly overshot the curb, crossed into the opposite lane, and crashed into a parked vehicle along the roadside.
The impact threw the rider off his motorcycle, and landed on the pavement.
He was rushed to the nearest hospital for his severe head injuries but was declared dead on arrival.
The police report did not indicate whether the rider was wearing a protective helmet, as required under Republic Act No. 10054, or the Motorcycle Helmet Act of 2009.
Meanwhile, police also reported that a 35-year-old female pedestrian died after she was struck by a motorcycle at around 7:30 p.m. while crossing a street in Barangay Plaza Aldea at Tanay town.
The woman sustained fatal injuries and was brought to a local hospital before being transferred to the Rizal Provincial Hospital System in Antipolo City. She was declared dead on arrival.
Police said the kin of those involved were working toward an amicable settlement. /apl

articles.title: UK support for Falkland Islands 'unwavering', No 10 says
articles.summary: The comments come as Argentinian president Javier Milei says the "winds of change" favoured his country's claim on the British overseas territory.

blocks.text: More than 40 years after the war over the territory, sovereignty of the archipelago in the south-west Atlantic Ocean remains hotly disputed between Britain and Argentina.
However in a 2013 referendum, residents of the islands voted overwhelmingly to remain a British overseas territory - with 99.8% voting in favour and just three voting against.

When asked about if the Prime Minister believed the UK had the necessary forces to defend the sovereignty of the islands the spokesperson said the they will remain so far as long as the islanders wish".
"Our armed forces are on standby 24/7 to protect the UK and our interests", the spokesperson added.
Announcing his plan for sanctions in a national address on Thursday, Milei reiterated that the Falkland Islands were "historically and legally" Argentinian.

Milei described the Sea Lion oilfield as a "clear and present danger", and said if Argentina does not act swiftly, "they will have the material capacity to access the oil that lies underneath our sea – something that has never happened before."

It is not yet clear how or to what extent the sanctions will be imposed or tightened. In Argentina, a current law already allows for restrictions of activities of oil companies participating in projects considered unauthorised on the islands.

Two oil companies – Britain's Rockhopper Exploration and Israel's Navitas Petroleum – are due to begin extracting oil in the Sea Lion oilfield off the Falklands coast within two years, something Milei said Argentina could not allow.
A joint statement from the two firms on Friday said it had the valid licences granted by the government of the Falkland Islands, "and with the full support of the UK government."
The project is due to deliver its first oil in 2028, Rockhopper and Navitas said the partnerships' timetable would not be affected.
The Sea Lion oilfield, around 130 miles from the islands, contains an estimated 1.7 billion barrels of oil - described by Rockhopper as a field containing "highly marketable crude".
On Thursday, President Trump hinted the US would not help the UK in any future Falklands conflict because Britain "had not been there to help me" during his war with Iran.
Trump's latest remarks on the islands come after he previously said the US position on the Falklands is one of many under review.
On Friday, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the UK would "resolutely uphold" the self-determination of the islands.
Writing on X on Friday, Miliband said the Islands would remain British as that is the "overwhelming position of the islanders."
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting also said Britain's commitment to the Falkland Islands was "absolute and unshakeable".
"Milei's statement overnight tells us more about domestic politics in Argentina than it does about the Falkland Islands," he wrote in his own post on X.
In an earlier statement, Downing Street said it was "not the first time" the Argentine government had made economic threats against the Falkland Islands.
"We are clear that the Falkland Islanders' right of self-determination extends to the right to exploit their own natural resources," it said.

articles.title: Two Reform UK officials resign amid donation breach reports
articles.summary: A Channel 4 report alleges that the party officials accepted foreign donations to fund three polls, illegal under the UK's electoral law. The allegations, which the party denies, come amid its annual…

image.caption: The hard-right, populist party's annual conference comes amid a dip in popularity fueled by similar scandalsImage: Temilade Adelaja/REUTERS

blocks.text: Reform UK's annual conference on Friday is being overshadowed by a fresh scandal, after a Channel 4 report alleged that the populist party flouted electoral laws by accepting foreign donations.
Senior party officials James Orr and Dan Jukes have stepped down following the allegations, and the party said it was launching an internal investigation.
The hard-right Reform denies wrongdoing, with leader Nigel Farage saying nothing illegal took place.

The allegations come at a time when the party is struggling with a dip in popularity fueled by similar scandals as well as the replacement of former British Prime Minister Keir Starmer with Andy Burnham.

Farage is due to address the conference and was hoping his speech would restore some of his popularity. Jordan Bardella, the leader of France's anti-immigrant, eurosceptic National Rally (RN) party, is also due to address the conference on Friday.
Where do Europe's far-right parties differ?
What are the latest allegations against Reform UK?
The Channel 4 investigation alleges that the two senior Reform figures had arranged for a US company to pay over £30,000 (roughly €35,000 or $40,570) for three party-commissioned opinion polls.
British laws on political funding ban foreign donations.
According to the investigation, the donors were in fact undercover reporters from an independent organization founded by journalists from the Center for Climate Reporting, called Verbatim.
Right-wing protesters clash with London police
Orr, the party's head of policy, said that Reform had not been involved in commissioning the poll.

"There's absolutely no way this could amount to a benefit or donation in kind at all," he said, "It wasn't internal party polling. It wasn't Reform UK's poll. It was a public poll arranged by an independent person paying an independent pollster, and those polls ​were published immediately for the general public."
Farage, 62, insisted in an interview with LBC radio that Reform had "broken no laws" and was the victim of "entrapment."
Reform's popularity dips ahead of annual conference
The latest scandal has overshadowed the party's annual conference in Birmingham, where Farage had hoped to turn the tide on a popularity dip mainly fueled by another scandal.

The veteran Brexit campaigner faces a parliamentary watchdog probe over a £5 million donation from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne in 2024 which he had failed to declare to parliamentary authorities.
Farage denies any wrongdoing, saying the sum was received before he was elected and was therefore not subject to declaration.

Still, the scandal has had an impact on Farage and his party's popularity, especially since the Labour party swapped leaders earlier in the summer, with Andy Burnham replacing Keir Starmer as the country's prime minister and in doing so, restoring some of the ruling party's popularity.
Farage is eyeing the top position after Reform managed to chalk up significant success at May local elections, prior to Starmer's departure.

articles.title: Cebu, Bohol anti-drug ops target 129 cannabis, ₱238K shabu
articles.summary: Authorities uprooted 129 fully grown marijuana plants in Toledo City, Cebu, and arrested a drug personality in a buy-bust operation that yielded around 35 grams of shabu in Tagbilaran City, Bohol, in…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Authorities uprooted 129 fully grown marijuana plants in Toledo City, Cebu, and arrested a drug personality in a buy-bust operation that yielded around 35 grams of shabu in Tagbilaran City, Bohol, in separate anti-illegal drug operations on Thursday, September 3.
The operations were conducted by the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency Regional Office 7 (PDEA 7), Philippine National Police (PNP) units and other law enforcement agencies.
Marijuana in Toledo
Around 11:08 a.m., combined law enforcement elements uprooted 129 fully grown marijuana plants from a cultivation site in Sitio Guincamote, Barangay Captain Claudio, Toledo City.
Authorities reached the site after an over eight-hour trek.
The operation stemmed from information provided by a confidential informant, followed by about one month of case buildup, according to authorities.

The operation involved personnel from the PDEA Cebu Provincial Office, Naval Forces Central, PNP Drug Enforcement Group–Special Operations Unit 7, Cebu Provincial Police Office–Provincial Intelligence Unit, CPPO–2nd Provincial Mobile Force Company, and Toledo City Police Station.
PDEA 7 identified the suspected cultivator as alias Gene, a resident of Barangay Captain Claudio, who fled the scene before authorities could arrest him.
The 129 marijuana plants had an estimated value of ₱25,800.

Representative samples of the seized plants were turned over to the PDEA 7 Regional Office Laboratory, while the remaining plants were burned on site following protocols established for the disposition of dangerous drugs.
Authorities said a case for cultivation of dangerous drugs under Section 16, Article II of Republic Act 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, will be filed against Gene.
Shabu in Tagbilaran
Later that day, around 5:24 p.m., authorities arrested another drug personality in a buy-bust operation at Purok 4, Barangay Bool, Tagbilaran City, Bohol.
The operation was conducted by the PDEA Bohol Provincial Office, Tagbilaran Police Station and Bohol Maritime Police.

Authorities acted on information from a confidential informant and conducted about one week of case buildup before the buy-bust operation.The suspect was identified as alias Kalaw, 38, unemployed and a resident of Barangay Tangnan, Panglao, Bohol.
Seized during the operation were three packs of shabu weighing around 35 grams, with an estimated average market value of ₱238,000.
Authorities also seized the buy-bust money and a cell phone.
Authorities said Kalaw had allegedly been disposing of around 50 grams of shabu weekly.
The seized dangerous drugs were turned over to the PNP Bohol Forensic Unit for proper disposition.
As of Friday, September 4, Kalaw remains in the custody of the Tagbilaran Police Station.
He is set to face charges for the sale and possession of dangerous drugs under Sections 5 and 11, Article II of Republic Act 9165.
The two operations resulted in the seizure of illegal drugs with a combined estimated value of ₱263,800, including the ₱25,800 worth of marijuana plants and ₱238,000 worth of shabu.

articles.title: DOH eyes shifting medicine budget to PhilHealth to curb expiries
articles.summary: The Department of Health (DOH) is considering shifting part of its budget for medicines and other commodities to PhilHealth to reduce stockpiling and prevent medicines from expiring unused.

blocks.text: The Department of Health (DOH) is considering shifting part of its budget for medicines and other commodities to PhilHealth to reduce stockpiling and prevent medicines from expiring unused.
Acting Health Secretary Edwin Mercado said the proposal is being studied amid concerns over the management of government medicine stocks.

“Isa sa pinag-iisipan namin, yung mga budget po namin for commodities ay ilagay na as additional subsidy for PhilHealth para po hindi na kami nag-stock up ng gamot at hindi na kami mag-expire ng ganoong kalaki.”

(One of the things we are considering is putting our budget for commodities into additional subsidies for PhilHealth so that we would no longer have to stockpile as much medicine and have such large amounts expire.)
Mercado said the DOH currently procures around 40% of its commodities centrally, while the remaining 60% is procured through its Centers for Health Development (CHDs).
He said the proposed approach could allow PhilHealth to shoulder more of the purchasing and benefit-delivery function instead of having the DOH maintain large inventories at the central level.

The proposal came during the Senate Finance Committee’s review of the DOH and its attached agencies’ proposed 2027 budget, where senators also raised concerns about medicine availability, access, and the government’s handling of stocks nearing expiration.
Preventing wastage
The discussion follows concerns raised in the hearing over millions of pesos worth of medicines and other medical supplies that have expired or are nearing expiry.
Mercado said the DOH is reviewing its procurement and supply-chain systems, including how medicines are forecast, purchased, distributed, and monitored.
Senator Raffy Tulfo on Friday accused the DOH of lying when it said that some expired medicines have been returned, as the senator showed images of some of them being "buried."
“Pinabaon yung mga gamot by the hundreds of millions. At meron pa pang disposal committee na binuo. So, bakit kayo nagsisinungaling sa taong-bayan?”
(Medicines worth hundreds of millions were allowed to go to waste. A disposal committee was even formed. So, why are you lying to the public?)
“Since I became senator…. Bakit walang palya na nagkakaroon ng mga gamot na nag-e-expire? Not only by the hundreds of millions, but by the billions of pesos. Bakit nangyayari ito?”
(Since I became senator, why is it that medicines keep expiring without fail? Not only by the hundreds of millions, but by the billions of pesos. Why does this happen?)
DOH Undersecretary Gloria Balboa, however, said during the hearing that she was "unaware" of this.
“Wala po akong aware doon sa pinabalik na nag-e-expire. ’Yun lang pong near expiry ang alam po namin na nasa TOR na kailangan po nilang palitan bago mag-expire,” she noted.

(I am not aware of those that were returned because they were expiring. What I know is that the near-expiry stocks are covered by the terms of reference requiring suppliers to replace them before they expire.)
Tulfo said the recurring expiration of medicines was particularly troubling amid reports of shortages in health facilities.
Tulfo also questioned the DOH’s procurement practices, alleging that some suppliers may have been favored in purchases involving medicines that were already nearing expiration.

He said he intends to seek a Senate Blue Ribbon Committee investigation into the matter and asked the DOH to provide historical data on medicine stocks that had expired in previous years.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Yeng Constantino says husband Victor doesn’t get jealous of Ryan Bang
articles.summary: Yeng Constantino clarified that her husband, Victor “Yan” Asuncion, does not get jealous of Ryan Bang, whose past with the singer recently resurfaced following an emotional moment at her concert.…

blocks.text: Yeng Constantino clarified that her husband, Victor “Yan” Asuncion, does not get jealous of Ryan Bang, whose past with the singer recently resurfaced following an emotional moment at her concert.

Constantino was asked during an ambush interview after the media conference for “The Voice Kids” on Friday, Sept. 4, in Quezon City, whether her husband minds that her and Bang’s courting history recently renewed attention online.

“Sana nga nagseselos eh,” she joked. “Hindi nya kasi personality. Talagang ano sya, very understanding. Kilalang kilala kasi ako ng asawa ko. Alam nya ‘yung pagkanta ko kay Ryan ay nangungulit lamang ako. Actually, mas nakaka-emphatize nga siya kay Ryan kaysa sa akin.”
Constantino said Asuncion and Bang are not close friends, but she hopes that one day, the three of them will get to hang out together.
The story stemmed from Constantino “Biyaheng Bente: 20th Anniversary Concert” on Aug. 28, where she serenaded Bang and recalled their “almost” romance from their early years in show business.
Constantino previously revealed that she had a huge crush on Ryan but felt hurt when he stopped pursuing her.
Bang, for his part, explained that he thought the singer was not interested in him as he admitted that he was also “financially incapable” of dating someone at the time.
After the concert, Bang became emotional during the Sept. 2 episode of “It’s Showtime” while recalling his experience at Constantino’s concert.
He thanked Vice Ganda for bringing him to the show, saying it brought back good memories.
Bang, who has since become single following his split from former fiancée Paola Huyong earlier this year, wondered whether he would ever find someone like Constantino again.
Constantino said she did not expect her playful interaction with Bang at the concert to have such an emotional impact, noting that now she feels slightly regretful about singing to him.

“I was being playful. Hindi ko nga rin po alam ang naging resulta ng aking aksyon. At nag-cost nga na maungkat ang mga sugat. I’m really regretful din in a way. Siyempre nakita mo yung tao na may mga naalala siya. Nakasakit sa kanya. Masakit. Kasi ako, parang nagbibiro ako. Hindi ako nakapag-isip ng maayos to consider his feelings,” she said.
The “Chinito” singer noted that she had already reached out to Bang to apologize.

“Nag-message na po kami sa kanya. Talagang grabe ang sorry ko sa kanya. Ang haba po ng mga nobelang messages namin ni Ryan. Patawarin nyo po ako. Sorry talaga. Hindi ko alam na ganito. And it was really vulnerable. I really apologized for triggering some memories or moments in life namin. I wasn’t very mindful also,” she said.
When asked about Bang’s remark that he hoped he would someday find someone like Constantino, the singer assured him that he would find love.
“Siyempre naman. Naku, makakahanap at makakahanap si Ryan. Hindi deserve ni Ryan na questionin niya ang kanyang worth,” she said.

“Sa pagkakakilala ko po kay Ryan, talagang napakabait po na tao. What a good man. God has perfect timing for everybody. He deserves to be loved, to be cared for, to be seen. He deserves all of that,” she expressed.
Meanwhile, Constantino is one of the new judges of “The Voice Kids,” alongside Gloc-9 and returning judge Julie Anne San Jose. The new season premieres on GMA on Sept. 13. /apl

articles.title: Serbia: How the funeral of Ratko Mladic is dividing a nation
articles.summary: As the Serbian government leaves the decision about Ratko Mladic's funeral arrangements to his family, international pressure on the country is mounting. How do Serbs feel about the matter?

image.caption: 'There is no small town in Serbia without at least one mural glorifying Ratko Mladic,' says Jasmina Lazovic, executive director of the Humanitarian Law CenterImage: Darko Vojinovic/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The body of the former Bosnian Serb army commander Ratko Mladic, who died last week in The Hague, where he was serving a life sentence for genocide and other war crimes in Bosnia and Herzegovina, has arrived back in Serbia.
Wrapped in the Serbian flag, Mladic's coffin was carried by members of the Serbian Armed Forces from the plane to a vehicle that transported his remains to the Military Medical Academy for autopsy.

Several groups of citizens gathered along the route from the airport to the hospital. Standing on overpasses, they greeted the motorcade carrying Mladic's body, holding banners that read "Thank you, General" and "Heroes never die."
Pro-government tabloids provided minute-by-minute coverage, referring to Mladic as a "Serbian general" and claiming that he had been "killed in The Hague."
A funeral with full state honors?

Ratko Mladic was sentenced in 2017 to life imprisonment by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia in The Hague for the genocide in Srebrenica, in which more than 8,000 Muslim men and boys were killed, the years-long siege of Sarajevo during the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and other war crimes, including the establishment of detention camps for non-Serb civilians and prisoners of war.

blocks.caption: The body of former Bosnian Serb wartime general Ratko Mladic (in the red van) was transferred to the Military Medical Academy for autopsy after being flown to Belgrade from The HagueImage: Darko Vojinovic/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Belgrade media report that Mladic will be buried in Belgrade on Monday. Justice Minister Nenad Vujic had previously announced that the funeral would be held with the highest state honors.
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic, however, says the decision will be left to the family.
Security agencies estimate that tens of thousands of people could attend the funeral.

"We will be there to provide all kinds of logistical and transport support and to maintain public order and security," said the president, adding, "It is very difficult to ensure and guarantee the safety of everyone."
Glorification that has continued for decades

For Jasmina Lazovic, executive director of the Belgrade-based Humanitarian Law Center, which has spent decades working on transitional justice and dealing with the past, none of this comes as a surprise.
She points to the long-standing glorification of Ratko Mladic in Serbia and his legacy.

"There is no small town in Serbia without at least one mural glorifying Ratko Mladic. The narrative that he was unjustly convicted has existed for years," she told DW. "Now a narrative has emerged that he was killed, despite the fact that he died at the age of 85 after suffering several strokes."

Lazovic says that these narratives suit the state leadership's portrayal of Serbia as a country that fought exclusively defensive wars and do not leave enough room for a discussion of the consequences of those wars and the victims they left behind — neither in the media nor in the education system and institutions.

"And there are hundreds of thousands of victims across Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Kosovo. Above all, these were crimes committed against civilians, crimes that left the countries of the region — particularly Bosnia and Herzegovina — with a completely transformed ethnic structure," she said.
Lazovic says that the list of victims also includes those who survived rape and torture, as well as those who were forcibly displaced. "The list is long, and our knowledge is limited," she added.
A general without a rank
The announcement that Mladic could be buried with the highest state honors drew swift responses from the international community.

"Glorification of war criminals is contrary to European values. There is no place for it either in EU member states or in candidate countries. I hope the government in Belgrade is aware of that," said European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos.

blocks.caption: Ratko Mladic was convicted of war crimes, including the 1992-95 siege of Sarajevo. This memorial features the names of 1,601 children killed during that siegeImage: Amel Emric/REUTERS

blocks.text: Aleksandar Vucic responded by accusing the West and the Hague Tribunal of blaming only Serbs for war crimes and failing to deliver justice for Serbian victims. But for now, he has officially left the decision on whether the deceased general will receive state honors to Mladic's family.

Jasmina Lazovic believes Vucic will once again take a pragmatic approach and that the final decision will depend on an assessment of what brings the authorities greater political benefit and what could cause greater damage.
She also points out that the issue is not only political, but legal.

"What is being overlooked here is the fact that Ratko Mladic was indeed a general, but he was sentenced to life in prison. Under the Law on the Serbian Armed Forces, anyone sentenced to more than one year in prison for a criminal offense loses their rank and, therefore, all the privileges that come with that rank," she told DW.
"If Ratko Mladic were buried with the highest state honors in accordance with the rank he held during the armed conflicts, that would be a direct violation of the law of this country," said Lazovic.
What do Serbs want?

On the question as to how they view Ratko Mladic, Serbian citizens interviewed by DW in several cities across the multi-ethnic autonomous province of Vojvodina expressed sharply differing views, ranging from those who are convinced that Mladic was unjustly convicted to those who accept the genocide designation without reservation.

blocks.caption: Mladic was also convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, where over 8,000 Muslim men and boys were killed in the summer of 1995Image: Samir Jordamovic/Anadolu Agency/IMAGO

blocks.text: "What was he supposed to do, let them kill all the Serbs? Thank you [Mladic], for everything," one man from Ruma told DW.
"For me, the matter was settled when the genocide verdict was handed down," said a student from Novi Sad.
But most people simply wave the question away. "I have enough of my own problems," said Svetlana from Zrenjanin.
Goran, from Novi Sad, believes that it is simply another political issue: "They've been making fools of us for years. Nothing is different now," he told DW.
Jasmina Lazovic believes that most Serbs are apathetic about the matter.

For her, this is a greater problem than just the pro-government media portraying Serbia as wanting to say goodbye to Mladic as a general. She argues that confronting Mladic's legacy and the past is essential if Serbian society is to move forward.

articles.title: Sask. Crown says killer engaged in 'vigilante justice' when he shot man in back of head
articles.summary: Craig Fox will find out later this month how many years he will spend in prison before he's eligible for parole. He was convicted earlier this year of the second-degree murder of Lee Bearsears on…

image.caption: Craig Fox, pictured, shot Lee Bearsears in the back of the head on Poundmaker Cree Nation in Saskatchewan on Oct. 15, 2023. (Craig Fox/Facebook)

blocks.text: WARNING: This article contains details of abuse.
Craig Fox shot Lee Bearsears in the back of the head and then dumped his body in a field on Poundmaker Cree Nation.
Now, Fox is waiting to find out how many years he will spend in prison until he's eligible for parole.
The 29-year-old was convicted of second-degree murder after a trial earlier this year in Battleford Court of King's Bench.
At Fox's sentencing hearing last week, Bearsears's family members talked about the grief, heartbreak and emptiness in their lives after he was murdered on Oct. 15, 2023. Bearsears was 31 years old.
His younger siblings spoke about the role he played in raising them, and said they didn't know where they'd be without him.
"He helped a lot of us, probably even you. I was mad at you, but now I'm just trying to survive, trying to survive this," Bearsears's mother told Fox.
One of his kokums (grandmothers) wrote in her victim impact statement that Bearsears "took care of us all."
"We trusted, and never for a minute thought you would or could hurt him in this way," she wrote. "Do you realize what you took from people? Do you realize you had no right to do what you did?"
The murder
Justice Rochelle Wempe's verdict, issued in May, details what happened on Oct. 15, 2023.

Fox was high on crystal meth and alcohol when he and others spent the day travelling around in Bearsears's borrowed truck. Around 8 or 9 p.m., they returned to Poundmaker Cree Nation, where Bearsears was waiting.
Fox and a friend, Preston Checkosis, picked up Bearsears. Checkosis was driving, Bearsears was in the front passenger seat and Fox was in the back, behind Bearsears.
Fox held a sawed-off rifle to the back of Bearsears's head and fired a single shot, intentionally killing him, Wempe found.
Bearsears's body was then left in a field and his truck was abandoned at a waste transfer station on the reserve.
Evidence at trial that Wempe noted included that Fox's DNA was found on the action of the rifle and his fingerprints were the only ones found in the passenger area of the vehicle.
Why did Fox kill Bearsears?
Comments Fox made after the shooting were also significant in Wempe's verdict.

In the hours after shooting Bearsears, Fox went to an aunt's house on Little Pine First Nation, just west of Poundmaker Cree Nation, where his brother and another cousin were staying. The cousin woke up and talked to Fox.
The cousin testified that when he asked Fox what was going on, Fox said, "We bodied a skinner" three or four times and "I bodied a skinner" one time.

Wempe said there was evidence that "skinner" is a slang term used to describe a child molester. The agreed facts in the trial included that Bearsears had been charged with sexual assault for allegedly inappropriately touching a young person.
Bearsears had pleaded not guilty and had a preliminary hearing scheduled for early 2024. Fox "became aware" of the allegation in September 2023, Wempe noted.

Police also found a message on Fox's phone sent on Jan. 19, 2024, from his Facebook profile that "stated that he had been sexually assaulted when he was younger and that he would put people who commit sexual assault 'under the dirt where they belong,'" Wempe said.
Sentencing positions
Second-degree murder carries an automatic sentence of life in prison with no chance of parole for a minimum of 10 years, and a maximum of 25 years.
The Crown argued for a period of parole ineligibility of 15 to 20 years, while the defence argued for 10 years.
In arguing for a lengthier period of parole ineligibility, Crown prosecutor Oryn Holm said Fox engaged in "vigilante justice" and acted as "judge, jury and executioner."
"Mr. Fox, in some irony, was found guilty after a trial. By his actions, he denied Mr. Bearsears the right to a trial," Holm said in court.
He said Bearsears had no expectation of violence on the night he died, no chance to defend himself, no chance to flee and his body was then "callously" left in a field.

items: Man gets 15 years for shooting Sask. woman after racial slur

blocks.text: Holm also referenced Fox's lengthy criminal record and the fact he was subject to a firearms prohibition when he murdered Bearsears.
Background factors
Defence lawyer Pamela Wayman, who represented Fox alongside Brent Little, argued that Fox's life "can't be understood apart from the intergenerational effects of colonial institutions."
His grandparents and his father attended residential schools and his mother attended a day school, giving rise to the violence and addiction that Fox was then exposed to at a very young age.
Fox "experienced displacement almost from birth," being placed in foster care as a baby. His childhood was marked by poverty, addiction, violence and severe abuse, Wayman said.

For a period of time, Fox lived with his father in Alberta, but said the abuse he experienced there made it the "worst days of his life." He repeatedly tried to run away, then ended up being placed in group homes, which Wayman said was a "pathway" to how he became involved with institutions and, subsequently, the justice system.

items: Supreme Court upholds woman's 1st-degree murder conviction in Tiki Laverdiere death

blocks.text: As a teenager, he disclosed "deeply personal information" to a counsellor in a group home, who then shared that information with staff and others in the home. That breach of trust had "significant consequences" for Fox, Wayman said. He stopped participating in counselling.
With more trustworthy counselling and support, Wayman said, Fox "may have developed healthier ways to manage his trauma and, later, stress."
He began using alcohol and drugs at a young age, sometimes supplied by older relatives.

All of those background factors — family history of residential school, intergenerational trauma, child welfare removal, separation from siblings and parents, institutional placement, poverty, addiction, childhood victimization, exposure to substances at an early age, disrupted education and early entrenchment in the criminal justice system — don't excuse the crime or diminish the harm to Bearsears's family, but must be given weight in sentencing, Wayman said.
When Wempe asked Fox if he had anything he wanted to say, he said he did not.
Wempe said she needed some time to consider the sentence. She is scheduled to give her decision on Sept. 25.

articles.title: Germany: Is Saxony-Anhalt's economy really struggling?
articles.summary: Germany's far-right AfD has long claimed that the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt has been left behind. Is that really the case? A closer look at the data offers some interesting insights.

image.caption: Germany's far-right AfD is projected to emerge as the clear election winner in Saxony-AnhaltImage: Klaus-Dietmar Gabbert/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Germany is watching the upcoming state election in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt with keen interest. Much of the attention is focused on the performance of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), whose state branch in Saxony-Anhalt has been classified by the domestic intelligence agency as "confirmed right-wing extremist."
According to opinion polls, the AfD could emerge as the clear election winner.

In the last state election in 2021, the AfD won around 20% of the vote and has since been the largest opposition party. The state is governed by a coalition of the Christian Democrats (CDU), the Social Democrats (SPD) and the Free Democrats (FDP), with Sven Schulze (CDU) serving as state premier.
Where does Saxony-Anhalt stand?
The AfD is campaigning on the claim that Saxony-Anhalt has been left behind — both socially and economically.
The unemployment rate in Saxony-Anhalt is higher than the national average, while median earnings for full-time employees are lower than across Germany as a whole.

Of Saxony-Anhalt's roughly 2.1 million residents, just under 800,000 are in jobs subject to social security contributions. The chemical industry has traditionally been one of the state's major employers and among the most productive sectors of the economy, particularly in the so-called chemical triangle around the cities of Leuna, Merseburg and Bitterfeld-Wolfen.
Machinery and plant engineering companies, including suppliers to the struggling automotive industry, also play an important role in the manufacturing sector.

The retail, transport and hospitality sector accounts for around one-fifth of jobs, including many positions in tourism. The Harz Mountains, the Luther cities of Wittenberg and Eisleben, and Quedlinburg, with its UNESCO World Heritage status, are key destinations.
Saxony-Anhalt's economy growing more slowly than the national average

The perception that the eastern German states have still not caught up with the former West German states appears to resonate with voters. The AfD has built broad support around this message, particularly among younger voters.

It is often claimed that pensions are lower in eastern Germany than in the West, but this is no longer the case. It is true, however, that the proportion of pensioners in Saxony-Anhalt is slightly higher than the national average. Many pensioners in the East also rely solely on their state pension, whereas many in the West receive company pensions or income from private retirement savings in addition to their state pension.

Partly because of its higher proportion of pensioners, Saxony-Anhalt has one of the lowest levels of economic output per capita in Germany, at just three-quarters of the national average. The state's economy has also generally grown more slowly than the national economy in recent years.
'Foreigners are to blame'

The AfD has also made immigration a central campaign issue in Saxony-Anhalt, warning of "too much immigration" and "foreign influence" — and appears to be gaining support with this message. This is even though, compared with other German states, relatively few non-Germans live there.
Although Saxony-Anhalt is one of Germany's economically weaker states, it has gained population in recent years, according to migration figures.
Since 2016, more non-Germans have moved to Saxony-Anhalt than have left. The net migration balance for German citizens has also been positive for the past six years.
At the end of 2025, foreign nationals accounted for around 9% of Saxony-Anhalt's population — roughly half the share in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany's most populous state.

The claim that "foreigners are living off taxpayers" is also misleading. Compared with other German states, Saxony-Anhalt has a relatively low proportion of foreign nationals among potential recipients of welfare benefits such as basic income support.

However far the political and economic reality may diverge from the bleak picture painted by extremist parties, particularly the AfD, one trend appears evident: Support for radical parties is becoming increasingly entrenched.

The two formerly dominant parties, the CDU and SPD, are bearing the brunt of this shift and steadily losing ground. The CDU is increasingly struggling to maintain its status as a broad-based mainstream party, while the SPD is edging closer to the 5% threshold, raising the prospect that it could eventually struggle to win seats in some state parliaments.
This piece was originally published in German.
Is Germany's weak economy boosting the right-wing AfD?

articles.title: Body of world's youngest traditional king returns home to Uganda amid succession row
articles.summary: King Oyo died in the US last week aged 34 after receiving treatment for an aggressive form of cancer.

blocks.text: Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja described him as a "symbol of unity" and praised his work raising awareness about HIV and Aids among young people.
Opposition MPs also paid tribute, with acting opposition leader Patrick Nsamba Oshabe saying: "Heritage and development were never rivals in his hands."
President Museveni has ordered an official burial for the monarch and national flags will fly at half-mast for three days around the funeral.

On Wednesday, the Tooro kingdom's Prime Minister, Calvin Armstrong Rwomiire Akiiki, said the king had asked officials not to disclose the seriousness of his illness because he believed he would recover and return to his people.
He said the monarch had hoped to return home for this year's Empango - the annual celebration of his coronation - on 12 September.
"He was confident in his recovery," Akiiki said.
His death has triggered uncertainty over the future of the monarchy as Oyo was not officially married.
But Akiiki has said the king had a young son, whose identity would be revealed later in accordance with Tooro customs.
President Museveni also said the king's mother, Queen Best Kemigisa, had told him that her son had left an heir.

But Charles Kamurasi, who is head of the Babiito royal clan from which Tooro's kings are chosen, said he knew nothing about the reported child, prompting an unusual public disagreement among senior figures in the kingdom.
Others within the royal clan have questioned why they were apparently unaware of the child.
"The prime minister is not supposed to talk about the king's heir. It is a cultural process," one royal clan member was quoted as saying by Uganda's state-owned New Vision newspaper.
"How can we, blood relatives, not know of the child, and the prime minister says he knows? That is totally out of order," the clan member added.
Akiiki has since appealed for the dispute to be dealt with privately, saying he wanted to meet other elders to resolve their differences.
"Words spoken in moments of grief can deepen divisions that may take years to repair," he warned.
The Ugandan government has also intervened, urging people not to spread speculation about the succession on social media.

Culture Minister Henry Tumukunde said Ugandans should rely on official information from the government and the Tooro Kingdom, adding that any dispute would be dealt with under law governing traditional and cultural leaders.
"The whole world is watching how Uganda mourns its king," he said, urging people to show "restraint and respect".
The Tooro Kingdom follows a hereditary system in selecting its monarch.
King Oyo ascended the throne in 1995 and became an international curiosity because of his young age.
Before his burial, a church funeral service will be held at a local church.
His body will then be carried in a traditional procession to the Karambi Royal Tombs, with burial is expected to be completed by 14:00 local time.
According to Tooro tradition, kings are not buried in the evening.

articles.title: Bong Go questions timing of arrest warrant vs VP Sara Duterte
articles.summary: Senator Christopher Bong Go on Friday questioned the timing of the issuance of the warrant of arrest against Vice President Sara Duterte over her grave threats case.

blocks.text: Published September 4, 2026 6:50pm
Senator Christopher Bong Go on Friday questioned the timing of the issuance of the warrant of arrest against Vice President Sara Duterte over her grave threats case.
Go, a known ally of the Duterte family, asked why the arrest warrant was only issued now, coinciding with the impeachment trial of the Vice President.
“Nagtataka lang po ako sa timing. ‘Yung timing ang pinagtataka natin,” he said in an ambush interview at the Senate.
(I’m just wondering about the timing. The timing is what I’m curious about.)

“Bakit ngayon? Bakit ngayon ‘yung panahon na ongoing ‘yung impeachment? Daming panahon pa noon eh, even before the impeachment. Even before the impeachment, pwede namang mai-file ‘yan. Bakit ngayon ‘yung timing, talagang nagkatugma? Ang tagal na noon,” he added.

(Why only now? Why was it only issued now when the impeachment is ongoing? There was a lot of time before. Even before the impeachment, that could have been filed. Why is the timing now, coinciding with the trial? That happened a long time ago.)
Regardless, Go expressed belief that Duterte will be able to overcome the challenges.
“Sanay naman po ‘yun si Vice President sa mga ganong sitwasyon. Ongoing nga po ‘yung impeachment eh. She can handle. I believe, kaya niya po po ‘yun,” he said.
(The Vice President is used to such situations. The impeachment is even ongoing. She can handle it. I believe she can do it.)
Senator JV Ejercito, meanwhile, was mum on the matter, saying he has to look into it first.
Asked if the arrest warrant has any effect with the impeachment trial, he said, “I would have to study it. Pasensya na, katatapos ko lang dito [sa hearing]. Tignan ko muna.”
(I would have to study it. Sorry, I just finished with the hearing. I'll look at it first.)
Atty. Paul Lawrence Lim, Duterte’s counsel for the grave threats cases, announced Friday afternoon that a Quezon City regional trial court has issued a warrant of arrest against the Vice President.
The Department of Justice (DOJ) also confirmed the information.

In early August, the DOJ filed three counts of grave threats against Duterte over her remarks that she hired an individual to kill President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former speaker Martin Romualdez, should an alleged plot against her succeed.
Prosecutors recommended the bail to be set at P120,000 per count.

Following this, Duterte filed a motion to quash on the ground of jurisdiction, arguing that she and other impeachable officers have limited procedural immunity while in office under the 1987 Constitution.
Duterte’s alleged grave threats against the President is also the basis of one of the Articles of Impeachment against her in the ongoing trial before the Senate impeachment court. — RSJ, GMA News
